symptom: `mxcli test tests` fails with `reading test directory: open .../locked: permission denied` and runs nothing when one subfolder (a locked folder, a root-owned folder in a mounted volume) cannot be read, although `tests/Sales/*.test.mdl` next to it is fine
cause: `walkTestTree` returned the `filepath.WalkDir` callback's `err` for every entry, so an error below the root became the whole walk's error and `ParseTestDir` returned it as a hard failure
insight: **Moving from a one-level `ReadDir` to a recursive walk turns every subfolder's error into the whole run's error unless errors below the root are made per-entry.** Only an error on the root is fatal; below it `onErr` appends a `FileError{Dir: true}` and the callback returns nil (WalkDir already skips the unreadable folder), so the run still goes red through `FileErrors` and keeps every readable test. Every consumer of `FileErrors` then needs the folder case worded as `could not be read`, not `failed to parse`. **Tests that run as root (CI, devcontainers) cannot see `chmod 000`, and Windows ignores it**: the real chmod test skips there, so the logic is also pinned by injecting the error through the `walkFunc` seam (`walkTestTreeWith`), which runs everywhere. The same walk now serves `testFilesMTime` (`--watch`), so discovery rules cannot drift between the parser and the change detector.
